title: On the gain of entrainment in stable linear control systems with a nonlinear output
summary: A control system admits a positive gain of entrainment (GOE) if entrainment to a periodic input yields a larger output, on average, than the output generated by the corresponding constant input with the same mean value. We analyze GOE in continuous-time stable linear control systems with a static nonlinear output map. Although linear systems with linear outputs have zero GOE, we show that a nonlinear output may generate a nontrivial GOE through the mismatch between the average output along the entrained periodic orbit and the output evaluated at the corresponding averaged equilibrium.
